title: Customer Network Policy Engine PRD (draft)
content:
Purpose and context:
This PRD draft defines a customer-facing Policy Engine for Private deployments that centralizes approval gates, audit event generation, and runtime networking policies for customer-managed networks (VPC, transit, on-prem). The product bridges two problems we repeatedly see in private customers: first, inconsistent, manual approval handovers when unlocking network connectivity and sensitive operations; second, opaque and difficult-to-export audit trails tied to individual networking and control-plane events.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Provide a policy evaluation plane that enforces approval gates (human and automated) for operations touching customer-managed networking and high-risk control-plane actions.
- Emit a consistent, exportable audit event schema for network and approval-related actions (immutable, tamper-evident).
- Allow customers to configure network-level policies (CIDR allowlists, NAT traversal policies, peering restrictions) alongside approval workflows that include role-based approvers and SLA timeouts.
- Integrate with customer KMS/HSM for audit log encryption-at-rest and support configurable retention/archival (S3-compatible or customer-hosted).
- Minimal latency impact on normal inference traffic; approval gating should not materially affect runtime SLOs for already-approved flows.

Non-goals:
- This PRD does NOT cover full identity or SSO design for every customer identity provider—assume standard OIDC/SAML integrations provided by platform sign-in.
- Not building a generic policy language for all Redwood features; focus scope on networking and control-plane operations relevant to Private deployments.

High-level user stories:
- As a customer security admin, I want to require two-person approval for enabling incoming peering from an external cloud account so that a second operator verifies the CIDR and tagging rules.
- As a platform operator at Redwood, I want an immutable audit trail of the approval decisions and the resulting network changes so I can support incident forensics and audits.
- As a compliance reviewer, I want to export all approval-related events for a date range into a signed, hashed archive for regulatory retention requests.

Requirements (functional):
1) Approval Gates and Workflows
  - Support approval policies tied to operation types (e.g., create-peering, change-route-table, open-ingress-port).
  - Each policy can express: required approver roles (e.g., customer-admin, redwood-sre), approval count (1 or 2), timeout (auto-escalate to specific role), and pre-checks (automated checks that can auto-approve).
  - Approvals must be recorded with approver identity, timestamp, justification text, related artefact IDs (e.g., peering-id, ticket id).
  - Web UI and API endpoints to submit approvals, view pending approvals, and attach artifacts (config diff, test results).

2) Policy Evaluation Engine
  - Runtime policy evaluator that runs pre-change and post-change checks. Pre-change checks are synchronous (block until decision); post-change checks can be asynchronous (audit and revert if necessary).
  - Policies are versioned and can be pinned per-customer. Rolling back to prior policy versions must be supported.

3) Audit Event Schema and Integrity
  - Define a consistent audit event schema across networking and approvals: fields include event_id, timestamp_utc, customer_id, tenant_id, actor_id, actor_role, action_type, object_type, object_id, change_summary (diff), approval_state, policy_version, request_trace_id, and cryptographic_hash.
  - Events must be append-only; the control plane should sign batches of events (customer or Redwood key) to make tampering evident.
  - Export APIs: on-demand archive (signed tarball) and streaming export to customer log endpoints (syslog/HTTPS/Kinesis/SQS).

4) Networking-specific controls and validation
  - Policy objects for: allowed_peer_accounts, allowed_cidr_ranges, prohibited_ports, required_tags (on peering attachments), and encryption-mandates.
  - Automated network validation checks: CIDR overlap detection, route-policy simulation, packet-path sanity checks (when possible), connectivity smoke tests via ephemeral probes.
  - Support a read-only network topology view in the Console that shows approved vs pending connections and highlights risky overlaps.

5) Data Protection & Retention
  - Support customer-configurable retention policies with minimum and maximum bounds (e.g., min 90 days, configurable up to 7 years for specific customers).
  - Integrate with customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest; for customers without KMS provide Redwood-managed encryption and clear contract language.
  - Redact sensitive fields on export if requested (e.g., internal IPs) and include an export manifest listing redaction policy applied.

6) Observability & SLOs
  - Track metrics: approvals/submission rate, approval latency percentiles, policy-evaluation latency, audit-export success rate, failed automated checks.
  - Alerts: stuck approvals > SLA, failed exports, policy-evaluation errors.
  - Tracing: correlate approval events with request_trace_id to enable full request->approval->network-change visibility.

APIs and Console UX (high level):
- REST API surface: /v1/policies (create/list/update/version), /v1/approvals (submit/list/approve/reject), /v1/audit-exports (start/status/download), /v1/network-validate (simulate).
- Console flows:
  - Network Setup: when a customer requests to attach a VPC/peer, Console displays the applicable policy, required approvers, and pre-check results.
  - Approvals Inbox: list of pending approvals with filters, quick-approve modal, and attached diffs/artifacts.
  - Audit Archive: UI to generate and download signed archives with retention metadata and redaction manifest.

Operational model and permissions:
- Approvals and policy edits should be logged as discrete, auditable actions and require separate permissions (e.g., can_view_policies vs can_edit_policies vs can_approve_network_changes).
- Default RBAC roles: owner (customer-admin), network-approver, security-approver, redwood-support. Allow custom role mapping to customer SSO groups.

Security considerations:
- All approval APIs and audit exports must require MFA for high-privilege roles.
- Ensure least-privilege service accounts used for network probes and export agents.
- Harden the event signing keys: support HSM backed keys for customers that request higher assurance.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Customer can create a policy that gates create-peering and requires one customer approver and one Redwood approver.
- Approval workflow available via Console and API with clear state transitions and audit entries for each action.
- Audit events emitted for all approval lifecycle events and network-change actions, with exportable signed archive.
- Basic network validation checks implemented: CIDR overlap and route simulation.
- Metrics emitted for approval latency and audit-export success; basic dashboards in Console.

Rollout plan and phasing:
- Phase 0 (alpha): internal testing with Redwood SRE and 2 trusted customers; limited to a subset of regions; manual exports only.
- Phase 1 (beta): public beta with 5 customers, add automated export endpoints and KMS integration.
- Phase 2 (GA): full tenancy support, retention controls, and HSM-backed key option for exports.

Open questions / design tradeoffs:
- Should we require cryptographic signing by default, or make it opt-in (impacts complexity and key management)?
- How much of network validation do we simulate vs require customer-provided test hooks for ephemeral probes?
- Export formats: gzipped JSONL vs parquet? Choose JSONL for simplicity but consider parquet for scale.
- How to reconcile approvals with delegated admin models (customer delegates to MSPs)?

Dependencies:
- KMS/HSM integration (security infra).
- Console components for inbox and archive UI (frontend).
- Serving runtime change hooks to emit pre/post network-change events (serving-runtime team).
- SSO/OIDC mapping for roles (platform-auth).

Next steps / immediate TODOs:
- Sync with SRE and security to finalize event schema (assigned: Aisha).
- Prototype signed archive generation and a manual export CLI (assigned: Diego).
- UX draft for Approvals Inbox and Diff modal (assigned: Priya).
- Schedule walkthrough with two pilot customers (Ops: Evelyn).

Appendix: example audit event (human-readable illustration)
- event_id: ev_20260201_0001
- timestamp_utc: 2026-02-01T15:12:03Z
- customer_id: cust_4321
- actor_id: alice@example.com (role: network-approver)
- action_type: approve_peering
- object_type: vpc_peering_connection
- object_id: pcx-0a1b2c3d4e
- change_summary: "Approved peering between cust-VPC (10.0.0.0/16) and Redwood-managed transit (172.20.0.0/16); tags verified: env=prod"
- approval_state: approved (approver_count:2)
- policy_version: v1.3.2
- cryptographic_hash: sha256:abc123...

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a draft intended to capture the scope and acceptance criteria. Expect follow-ups to tighten event schema and finalize retention SLAs. Please add comments inline in Confluence and link relevant tickets.
